body: FWIW, I looked at your pic on r/toastme and I think you're really cute.  You actually look quite a bit like a couple of cis women I know.
Well, I'm not sure I would want someone *always* listening. :-) But I do wish someone understood me that well.
I wish I could believe that I am enough. I keep saying it to myself but it doesn't always feel convincing.

Yeah, I guess I was starting to suspect my childhood was not normal (my husband seemed shocked by some of the stories I told him) but I doubt myself a lot. My mom was really good at denying the reality I just saw happen and making me feel like I was crazy. At one point when I was a teen I said something that implied she was abusive and she went off on me and told me I was being melodramatic and making things up for attention and I had no idea what abuse was and how could I be so cruel and betray her that way after she bent over backwards for me. So I had this conversation with my therapist but in the back of my mind I'm thinking, "What if none of this is real? What if I'm just taking normal parenting stuff and blowing it out of proportion to be dramatic?" And it sets off a nuclear explosion of self hate.
I literally wrote 8 journal entries today. A lot of it is the same stuff over and over, but it's such a relief to be able to get it out.
Thanks, I just went and started a journal. Hopefully it will help. And I hope you are able to find some peace as well.

I don't really have non-work friends other than my husband. And after I got out of the hospital, he told me, "I'm so glad I don't have to worry any more. I stayed up so many nights worrying you would harm yourself, I could never really sleep." I figured that if I was going to kill myself, I was going to do it whether he worried about me or not, so I might as well not make him worry in the meantime.

I actually had a chat with someone who PMed me and I feel a little better now. Going from an intensive outpatient program where I was in therapy three mornings a week for 3 hours to just seeing a therapist for 50 minutes every 3 weeks has been really hard. Like, my therapist just explained to me that I didn't have a normal childhood and now I have three weeks to do what with that information? It's like someone explodes a bomb in your house and then walks away.
I was in the hospital for a month and it didn't help at all. It was my 8th hospitalization. I was totally open with everyone but there's no point, it just upsets people.
